differences.title: 1. Routing
differences.leftDesc: Layouts and loading states are collocated with routes, enabling easier UI composition and shared layouts.
differences.rightDesc: Component-based routing with nested routes, layouts, and dynamic segments for flexible routing patterns.

differences.title: 2. Data Loading
differences.leftDesc: Data is fetched within route segments, simplifying data fetching logic and error handling.
differences.rightDesc: Data fetching often handled at the page level, requiring explicit configuration for different rendering strategies.

differences.title: 3. Mutations
differences.leftDesc: Handles form submissions and data mutations directly within route modules, streamlining backend interactions.
differences.rightDesc: Requires separate API routes for handling mutations and backend logic, adding complexity.

differences.title: 4. Rendering
differences.leftDesc: Primarily server-rendered, focusing on progressive enhancement and a robust client-side fallback.
differences.rightDesc: Supports SSR, SSG, ISR, and Client-Side Rendering, offering flexible deployment options.

differences.title: 5. Form Handling
differences.leftDesc: Leverages native HTML forms and browser behavior for enhanced accessibility and performance.
differences.rightDesc: Often requires custom form handling or libraries for optimal performance and UX.

differences.title: 6. Progressive Enhancement
differences.leftDesc: Designed with progressive enhancement as a core principle, ensuring functionality without JavaScript.
differences.rightDesc: Requires explicit implementation to achieve full progressive enhancement benefits.

differences.title: 7. State Management
differences.leftDesc: Focuses on server state, minimizing client-side JavaScript for faster initial loads.
differences.rightDesc: Offers robust client-side state management options alongside server-side solutions.
